I couldn’t verify a diaper brand/product specifically called **“Wiggle & Snug Snug-Fit Diapers”** from reliable sources, so I’d double-check the exact name on the package. If you meant **Huggies Little Snugglers** or **Huggies Snug & Dry**, then **yes, they can be suitable for newborns** as long as you choose the newborn size and the fit is right.

**What to look for for a newborn:**

- **Correct weight range:** Newborn diapers are typically for babies up to about **10 lb**; Huggies Little Snugglers newborn is listed as **up to 10 lb**. ([target.com](https://www.target.com/p/-/A-15145170))  
- **Gentle materials:** For sensitive newborn skin, it’s a plus if the diaper is **fragrance-free, hypoallergenic, and free of lotions/parabens**; Huggies Little Snugglers is described this way, and Huggies Snug & Dry is also listed as fragrance-free and hypoallergenic. ([target.com](https://www.target.com/p/-/A-15145170))  
- **Umbilical cord area:** A newborn diaper with an **umbilical cord opening/cutout** is helpful in the first couple of weeks; Huggies Little Snugglers newborn lists this feature. ([target.com](https://www.target.com/p/-/A-15145170))  
- **Not too tight:** A “snug fit” is good only if it doesn’t leave red marks or trap moisture. The AAP notes that diapers fastened too tightly can contribute to rubbing, irritation, and diaper rash. ([healthychildren.org](https://www.healthychildren.org/English/tips-tools/ask-the-pediatrician/Pages/Why-is-my-baby-always-getting-diaper-rashes.aspx))  

**Bottom line:** They’re likely fine for a newborn **if they’re fragrance-free, absorbent, newborn-sized, and not too tight**. If your baby gets redness, leaks, blowouts, or marks around the legs/waist, try fastening looser or size up/down. For persistent rash or worsening irritation, ask your pediatrician.
